learning_outcomes.text: Understands ex-technical aspects of the activities included in the profession of a mechanical engineer, among others its social impact and influence on the condition of an environment; is aware of the responsibility connected with the decisions made in connection with engineering activity. Student lists pollutants emitted into the atmosphere. Student defines and distinguishes between waste and hazardous waste. Student lists basic legislation on environmental protection.

Possesses basic knowledge necessary to understand the ex-technical conditions of engineering activity, possesses basic knowledge on management, including quality management and running commercial enterprise, within the range of protection of intellectual property and patent law; knows general principles of creating and developing forms of individual entrepreneurship and basic HSE rules applicable to machine industry. The student has basic knowledge of environmental management and ecology necessary to understand the non-technical aspects of engineering activity. They are familiar with the fundamental principles of sustainable development, environmental protection, and the impact of industrial activity on ecosystems. The student understands the importance of quality management, occupational safety, and environmental responsibility in engineering and business practice.

The student is able to analyze the environmental impact of devices and technical systems and compare selected design solutions using functional, safety, environmental, economic, and legal criteria. They can assess their compliance with the basic principles of environmental protection and sustainable development. The student is able to identify more environmentally friendly solutions and justify their selection.

syllabus_topics: Effect of Global Warming on Climate Change
Pollution and Causes of Climate Change
Effect Of Using Fossil Fuels On Climate Change
Hydro power, Wind power, Geothermal Energy, Solar Power, Biomass, Nuclear energy
assessment_rules: The passing threshold for weekly reports is 56.0%.
bibliography: A. Farmer. Handbook of Environmental Protection and Enforcement. Principles and Practice. Earthscan. London. 2007
D.H.F. Liu, B.G. Liptak, P.A. Bouis. Environmental Engineers Handbook. Lewis Publishers. 1997.
F.R. Spellman. Handbook of Environmental Engineering. CRC Press. 2015.
degree: Mechanical Engineering, first-cycle (engineer), specialization Design and Production Engineering
